newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BT says export data suggest higher NZ June qtr GDP.
newsitem.headline: BT says export data suggest higher NZ June qtr GDP.

text.p: Bankers Trust New Zealand economists said on Wednesday a 6.2 percent rise in export volumes between the 1995 and 1996 June quarters suggested stronger June quarter GDP growth.
"We are likely to revise our current estimate (0.4 percent) up closer to one percent," they said in a commentary on June quarter terms of trade data published earlier by Statistics NZ.
"However, with growth driven from the low-inflation tradeables sector, and the terms of trade not generally a market focus, we think today's result is neutral for financial markets."
SNZ said New Zealand's terms of trade index fell 0.7 percent from the March to June quarters. Export volumes were up 6.2 percent on a year ago, while import volumes were up 0.1 percent.

BTNZ said the likelihood of stronger GDP growth should not raise fears of higher inflation. For a given June quarter employment increase of 0.9 percent, stronger GDP growth would imply better productivity.

However, it noted the annual falls of 1.4 percent and 0.7 percent in export and import prices respectively were less than might be expected given the 6.4 percent rise in the New Zealand dollar Trade-Weighted Index over the same period.

The economists said import orders for July, at $1.5 billion, were somewhat weaker than expected and orders for consumer goods were sluggish for the second month. The data supported the picture of a slowing economy, though not conclusively.
